newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH GOVERNMENT TO BOOST ORGANIC FARMING SECTOR.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH GOVERNMENT TO BOOST ORGANIC FARMING SECTOR.

text.p: The Dutch government said on Tuesday it would provide extra funds to boost the fledgling organic farming sector in a bid to catch its more developed European neighbours such as in Denmark and Austria.

"The aim is to get more organic foodstuffs into the shops and the government will now provide extra money for this," a spokesman for the ministry of agriculture said, adding that a decision will be taken on the amount involved this autumn.
The Netherlands now has around 600 farms devoted to organic methods, but only about 0.6 percent of the total in the country. Around 12,000 hectares is given over to organic production.
This is way behind countries such as Austria and Denmark where the proportion of organic production is nearer 10 percent.
The spokesman said the government was also encouraging a dialogue between supermarket chains and individual organic growers to get more produce into the shops.
"The main problem is that organic food at the moment is only available in specialist shops," he said.
